description.narrative:
Project description / activities (including numbers to be reached):
This project is an emergency drought response designed to address acute food insecurity in Northern Galkayo, Mudug region, where prolonged drought and repeated rainfall failure have pushed largenumbers of households into IPC Phase 3 and Phase 4 conditions. Following the national drought declaration in late 2025 and the poorperformance of the Deyr rains, households are facing severe food shortages, rising staple food prices, livestock losses, and increased displacement risks. With no rains expected before April 2026, immediate food assistance is critical to prevent further deterioration during the peak Jilaal dry season.
Implemented by Oxfam’s Puntland office in coordination with local authorities and communitystructures, the project targets Northern Galkayo, one of the districts most affected by drought and food insecurity. The intervention prioritises the most vulnerable households, including women- and elderly-headed households, families with malnourished children, households with people living with disabilities, and marginalised communities. The CAT Fund rapid response will reach 818 households(approx. 4,909 people).
The project objective is to stabilise household food consumption and prevent the use of harmful coping strategies through timely cash-for-food assistance. A total of 818 vulnerable households will receive two rounds of cash transfers overtwo months, with each household receiving USD 55 per month (GBP 41.55).The transfer value is aligned with the Somalia Food SecurityCluster recommended transfer value, using the reduced 70 percent Minimum Expenditure Basket for Mudug region. Assistance will be delivered in January and February 2026, with Oxfam actively seeking additional funding to extend support beyond the CAT Fund period where possible.
Cash has been selected as the most appropriate modality for food assistance in Northern Galkayo. Markets remain functional, and cash enables households to access staplefoods quickly and according to their needs. Cash transfers are faster to deliver than in-kind food, preserve dignity, reduce logistical costs, and support local markets while ensuring households can prioritise food consumption during the most critical period of the drought. Oxfam has existing framework agreement with mobile money transfer service provider in Puntland.
Key Activities
1. Coordination, stakeholders – including community engagement Engage district authorities, community leaders, and relevant coordination mechanisms to introduce the project, confirm target locations, and ensure alignment with drought response priorities. Conduct community meetings to explain project objectives, food-only entitlements, selection criteria, timelines, andfeedback and complaints mechanisms. Establish or activate inclusive Community Committees in each target location, ensuring at least 50 percent women’s representation and inclusion of marginalized groups. Committees will be oriented on fair, protection-sensitive targeting.
2. Household listing and targeting Prepare preliminary beneficiary lists using agreed vulnerability criteria, prioritizing households affected by displacement, female- or elderly-headed households, families with malnourished children, households with people living with disabilities, and those without sustainable livelihoods.
3. Registration and verification Register selected households and conduct two-stage verification led by Oxfam programme and MEAL teams to validate eligibility and ensure assistance reaches the most food-insecure households.
4. Final beneficiary validation Consolidate and validate final beneficiary lists jointly with community committees and local authorities to strengthen transparency and accountability.
5. Cash transfer delivery Deliver two rounds of cash-for-food assistance through a secure mobile money transfer service provider, providing USD 55 per household per month to 818 households in January and February 2026.
6. Monitoring, accountability, and safeguarding Monitor transfers and food access outcomes, operate feedback and complaints mechanisms, and apply safeguarding and protection standards throughout implementation.
In parallel, the project includes a focused communication component to document and raise awareness of the drought and worsening food insecurity in Puntland. In collaboration with the Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA), Oxfam will support field-based documentation of drought impacts, food access constraints, and household coping strategies. Outputs will include photographs, short human-interest stories, and short video clips, which will be used to inform donors, humanitarian partners, and the wider international community. This activity aims to strengthen evidence-based visibility of the crisis and support broader resource mobilisationfor the drought response.

participating-org.narrative: In 2004 Oxfam Novib set up a Liaison Office in Nairobi, Kenya in order to support the Strengthening Somali Civil Society Program, at the request of the EU. This request was based on Oxfam Novib's work in Somalia to date, but intended to be more widely directed atthe entire civil society sector and the specific context in which it is operating in a post-conflict country. The program started with consulting local organisations in Somalia and Somaliland to get a complete picture of the sectors and regions where they are active, the challenges they face and the relationship between civil society, local political structures and the private sector. A program was then developed to strengthen the institutional development of Oxfam Novib's partners and those of other Oxfams, as well as a range of new NGOs. In the first year local consultants were trained in Somalia. They were then seconded to civil society organisations to build their capacity in financial and organisational management. Furthermore, workshops were organised on specific themes suchas human rights and the role of civil society in the Somali context. The Liaison Office is now going to support the expansion of the program, focussing on strengthening both organisation and project management, while facilitating more training in the fields of civic education, governance, human rights and women's rights, HIV and AIDS and child protection. Over the years, the Somalia Country Office has expanded its intervention on short term humanitarian response as well as development development interventions. In 2015/2016, a decision was reached to move the Country Programme operation, which was largely in Nairobi, from Nairobi to Hargeisa. The country office has a small office in Nairobi , Kenya and large operations office in Hargeisa, Somaliland.
